question:
(i) What happens when the impact parameter of an incident $\alpha$-particle is zero?
(ii) What does this case tell about the repulsive force between the $\alpha$-particle and the nucleus?

options.A:
(i) The alpha particle passes through the nucleus without deflection.
(ii) This proves there is no electrostatic force.
options.B:
(i) The alpha particle is scattered through a small angle.
(ii) The repulsive force is minimum because the particle is closest to the nucleus.
options.C:
(i) The alpha particle is absorbed by the nucleus.
(ii) The force becomes attractive.
options.D:
(i) For zero impact parameter, the alpha particle approaches the nucleus head-on, momentarily stops at the distance of closest approach and retraces its path.
(ii) Since both are positively charged, the direct electrostatic repulsion is maximum and produces maximum deflection.
